title: DATS Test File
description: Schema for Declarative Automated Testing System (.dats) files

$schema.description: Optional reference to this JSON Schema

setup.description: File-level setup: command(s) run once, in order, before any of the file's tests, after shared files are written. Only {shared.X} placeholders are expanded. If a command fails, the remaining setup commands are skipped and EVERY test in the file is reported as failed (never as skipped); teardown still runs.

teardown.description: File-level teardown: command(s) that always run once, in order, after the file's tests -- after test failures and even when setup failed. One failing command does not stop the rest, but any failure marks the file failed (exit 1) even when all tests passed. Only {shared.X} placeholders are expanded.

tests.description: Array of test cases (at least one; the runner rejects an empty array)

commandList.description: One setup/teardown entry (see hookCommand), or an ordered list of them (at least one).

hookCommand.description: A setup/teardown command: a bare command string (no extra env, no stdin, the default 30s timeout), or a mapping with cmd plus optional env, stdin_file, and timeout. Runs via bash -c like a test cmd. cmd and env values expand {shared.X} only; {inputs.X}/{outputs.X} are per-test namespaces and stay verbatim here. Blank commands are rejected at parse time, as is a shell heredoc (<<WORD) -- write the file and pull it in with shared.files/shared.copy instead -- and a herestring (<<<), which should be inputs.stdin (or stdin_file) or a pipe instead.

env.description: KEY=VALUE entries added to this command's environment; values expand {shared.X} only.

stdin_file.description: A host file whose raw content is piped to the command's stdin, unexpanded. A relative path resolves against the directory holding this .dats file.

timeout.description: This entry's own timeout bound, in place of the default (30s). An integer number of seconds, or a Go duration string (e.g. "500ms", "2s"); either form must be greater than 0 -- there is no way to spell "no timeout" for a hook command.

shared.description: File-level shared fixtures, written once into the file's shared directory before setup runs. Tests address them with {shared.X} placeholders and should treat them as read-only.

files.description: Shared fixture files to create once per file, mapping filename to content. Contents go through {shared.X} placeholder expansion only. File names must be relative paths that stay inside the shared directory (no ".." or absolute paths; rejected at parse time); nested paths like "sub/file.txt" are allowed. The shared block must declare at least one entry across files and copy combined; a name may appear in only one of the two.

additionalProperties.description: File content ({shared.X} placeholders are expanded; {inputs.X}/{outputs.X} stay verbatim)

copy.description: Host files to copy once per file into the shared directory, writable. Maps destination filename to a host source path; a relative source resolves against the directory holding this .dats file. Destination names follow the same locality rule as files and must not also appear there. {matrix.X} is not substituted here.

additionalProperties.description: Host source path to copy from (relative paths resolve against the .dats file's directory)

sandbox.description: File-level sandbox settings for every command this file runs (its tests AND its setup/teardown hooks). The CLI sandboxes commands by default (--sandbox=auto: bubblewrap, falling back to docker); this block can narrow that choice for one file, never widen it. Write `false` to opt the file out entirely -- the declarative counterpart of --no-sandbox, for files whose commands genuinely need the host. Under --sandbox=none the whole block is inert.

oneOf.description: false opts this file out of sandboxing; true is the explicit opt-in, identical to omitting the key

enabled.description: Whether this file's commands are sandboxed (default true). false is the same opt-out as `sandbox: false`.

network.description: Whether sandboxed commands keep network access (default true). false runs them in an empty network namespace (bwrap) or with --network none (docker).

image.description: Container image the docker backend runs this file's commands in, overriding --sandbox-image. Ignored by the bwrap backend, which uses the host's own filesystem. The image must provide bash.

desc.description: Optional description of the test case

cmd.description: Command to execute (via bash -c). {inputs.X} expands to the absolute path of the declared input file X; {outputs.X} expands to an absolute path in the test's private outputs directory (no outputs.files check required); {shared.X} expands to an absolute path in the file's shared directory (no declaration required). The same expansion is applied to inputs.files contents. When the test declares a matrix, {matrix.X} is substituted first (plain text, one instance per value combination). A shell heredoc (<<WORD, <<-WORD, <<~WORD) is rejected at parse time -- write the file and pull it in with inputs.files/inputs.copy or shared.files/shared.copy instead -- and so is a herestring (<<<), which should be inputs.stdin or a pipe instead.

exit.description: Expected exit code (0-255, bare or quoted) or exit code name (default 0)

oneOf.$comment: Only the names the runner resolves (EXIT_SUCCESS=0, EXIT_FAILURE=1); any other EXIT_* name is rejected at parse time because it could never pass a run.

oneOf.description: A quoted integer exit code (e.g. "3"), accepted as its numeric value; the 0-255 range is enforced at parse time

timeout.description: Optional per-test timeout: an integer number of seconds, or a Go duration string (e.g. "500ms", "2s", "1m30s"). A bare integer (quoted or not) means seconds. 0 or omitted means no timeout.

oneOf.description: A Go duration string (e.g. "500ms", "2s", "1m30s"), or a quoted bare integer meaning seconds

matrix.description: Matrix (parameterized) test: a mapping of variable name to a list of scalar values, expanding the test into one instance per combination (cartesian product). Variables keep declaration order and the LAST variable varies fastest; instances report as "desc [k=v, k2=v2]" and EVERY instance always runs (dats has no test filtering or selection). {matrix.X} substitutes -- in a single pass, before any runtime placeholder expansion -- into desc, cmd, inputs.stdin, inputs.files contents, inputs.env values, all output pattern strings, and every string scalar inside json_output; fixture file names, env var names, exit, timeout, and the matrix block itself stay literal. References to undeclared variables, and matrix placeholders in setup/teardown commands or shared file contents, are rejected at parse time.

additionalProperties.description: The variable's values (at least one). Each value must be a scalar -- string, number, or boolean -- substituted as its literal YAML text (1.50 stays "1.50", true stays "true"). Duplicate values (compared after stringification, so 1.50 and "1.50" collide) are rejected at parse time.

stdin.description: Content piped to the command's stdin. Never placeholder-expanded at runtime, but {matrix.X} IS substituted at instance-expansion time when the test declares a matrix.

files.description: Fixture files to create before running, mapping filename to content. Contents go through the same {inputs.X}/{outputs.X}/{shared.X} placeholder expansion as cmd. File names must be relative paths that stay inside the test directory (no ".." or absolute paths; rejected at parse time); nested paths like "sub/file.txt" are allowed. A name must not also appear under copy.

copy.description: Host files to copy into the test's input directory before running, writable. Maps destination filename to a host source path; a relative source resolves against the directory holding this .dats file, with {matrix.X} substituted first when the test declares a matrix. Destination names follow the same locality rule as files and must not also appear there.

additionalProperties.description: Host source path to copy from (relative paths resolve against the .dats file's directory; {matrix.X} substitutes first)

env.description: Environment variables for the command, mapping name to value. The variables are ADDED to the inherited environment (appended in sorted key order; they do not replace it). Values go through the same {inputs.X}/{outputs.X}/{shared.X} placeholder expansion as cmd.

stdout.description: Stdout checks. Array form: literal substrings that must each appear anywhere in stdout. Map form: 0-indexed line number to regex that must match (unanchored search) within that line; addressing a nonexistent line fails.

stderr.description: Stderr checks. Array form: literal substrings that must each appear anywhere in stderr. Map form: 0-indexed line number to regex that must match (unanchored search) within that line; addressing a nonexistent line fails.

!stdout.description: Negated stdout checks. Array form: literal substrings that must NOT appear anywhere in stdout. Map form: 0-indexed line number to regex that must NOT match (unanchored search) within that line; a nonexistent line passes.

!stderr.description: Negated stderr checks. Array form: literal substrings that must NOT appear anywhere in stderr. Map form: 0-indexed line number to regex that must NOT match (unanchored search) within that line; a nonexistent line passes.

files.description: Output file validations, mapping filename to checks. File names must be relative paths that stay inside the test directory (no ".." or absolute paths; rejected at parse time); nested paths like "sub/file.txt" are allowed.

!files.description: Negated output file validations, mapping filename to checks. Each check is inverted: exists is flipped (exists: true means the file must NOT exist), match patterns must NOT match the contents (a missing file passes), and notMatch patterns MUST match the contents (a missing file fails). File names must be relative paths that stay inside the test directory (no ".." or absolute paths; rejected at parse time); nested paths like "sub/file.txt" are allowed.

snapshot.description: Golden-file (snapshot) assertion: captured output must byte-match a stored golden file. Goldens live in a .snapshots directory next to the .dats file (<file>.snapshots/NNN-<slug>.<stream>.golden, named by the canonical 1-based instance number and the slugged instance name, matrix label included). Comparison is byte-exact after normalization: framework temp paths are replaced with the stable tokens {testdir}, {shareddir}, and {tmproot} so goldens are reproducible across runs. A missing or differing golden fails the test; running with --update rewrites goldens from actual output (and prunes stale ones) instead.

oneOf.description: true snapshots stdout; false is the documented toggle-off, identical to omitting the key
Per-stream form: which output streams to snapshot (each stream gets its own golden file). At least one stream must be enabled -- a mapping that enables neither is rejected at parse time.

stdout.description: Snapshot the captured stdout against the instance's .stdout.golden file

stderr.description: Snapshot the captured stderr against the instance's .stderr.golden file

json_output.description: Expected JSON value of the whole stdout. Stdout must parse as a single JSON value that deep-equals this value: object keys are order-insensitive, array elements are order-sensitive, numbers compare by value (2 == 2.0). Any JSON value is allowed here, including null (which asserts stdout is exactly the JSON null).

outputCheck.description: Output validation - either an array of literal substrings or a map of line-specific regex checks

oneOf.description: Literal substrings matched anywhere in the whole output. NOT regexes - metacharacters have no special meaning.

Map of 0-indexed line numbers to Go/RE2 regexes. Each regex is searched UNANCHORED within its line - use ^...$ to pin the whole line. Positive checks fail when the addressed line does not exist; negated checks pass.

fileCheck.description: Validation for an output file. An empty check ({} or null) is an implicit existence assertion: under files the file must exist, under !files it must NOT exist.

match.description: Go/RE2 regex patterns that must match the file's contents (under !files: must NOT match; a missing file passes there)

notMatch.description: Go/RE2 regex patterns that must NOT match the file's contents (a missing file passes; under !files: MUST match, and a missing file fails)
